title: Give the row components their list ancestor so they isolate faithfully
description:
Two component scenarios were capturing a component that was not really the component. ElsewhereRow and SocialRow each render a bare `<li><a>`, and essentially all of their layout is written against the list their parent renders — `.rows li` / `.rows a` for one, `.socials li` / `.socials a` for the other. Isolated without that ancestor, the descendant selectors matched nothing: the anchor stopped being a grid (or a flex row), so ElsewhereRow's four columns collapsed into a single run-on line reading "DISCUSSIONPairing with Claude Code…Hacker News · 178 points2025", SocialRow lost the left/right split between name and handle, both lost the rules above and below, and ElsewhereRow regained the list bullet that `.rows`'s `list-style: none` had been suppressing.

The captures were not blank and did not error, which is why this survived: the screenshots showed real content, and the audit's screenshot-coverage check only asks whether a capture is fresh, not whether it is faithful. They read as broken tiles in the gallery rather than as failures.

Both isolation pages now supply the list ancestor. ElsewhereRow wraps its row in `<ul className={styles.rows}>`. SocialRow already had a `<ul>`, but an unclassed one carrying inline `listStyle: none` — enough to hide the bullet, which is exactly what made the omission look intentional, and not enough to bring the layout with it; it now uses `styles.socials` and overrides only the two-column track, since the section pairs rows across two columns and a single isolated row should occupy the width of one.

These are the only two components with this shape. Every other class carrying descendant rules on bare tags — `.links`, `.posts`, `.facts`, `.nav`, `.signoff`, `.chip`, `.confirm`, `.failure`, `.mark`, `.cities` — is rendered by the same component that renders the children beneath it, so those isolate correctly on their own.
